SELECTED_INDEX: 1  
CONFIDENCE: 0.27  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows only aliphatic C–H stretches at 2877, 2936 and 2980 cm⁻¹ (rule GFQ-003) and a single CH₂/CH₃ deformation at 1462 cm⁻¹, indicating an aliphatic molecule containing both CH₃ and CH₂ groups but no C=C, C≡C or aromatic rings. The three closely-spaced C–O stretching region bands at 1048, 1087 and 1125 cm⁻¹, together with the 1277 cm⁻¹ band, match the typical strong C–O and C–C–O vibrations of alcohol/ether systems such as ethoxy and hydroxyethyl groups. The 892 cm⁻¹ (CH₂ rocking) and 834 cm⁻¹ (C–C–O deformation) peaks are characteristic of simple alkoxy alcohols like ethanol and 2-ethoxyethanol. Among the candidates, only 1 (CCOCCO, 2-ethoxyethanol) possesses one ethyl group (CH₃–CH₂–), an –O– linkage, and a terminal –OH, exactly the functional groups needed to give the observed CH₃/CH₂ and multiple C–O related Raman bands. Candidates containing N (2, 4, 5) should show N–H or NO stretches (rule GFQ-022) that are absent, while larger, more branched ethers (3, 6, 7, 10) would introduce extra strong CH₃ deformation bands (~1375 cm⁻¹) not seen in the top peaks. Methanol (9) lacks CH₂-related bands at 892 and 1462 cm⁻¹. Therefore candidate 1 best fits the experimental Raman features.
